title: 第四节论因集推理的组成部分

content.value:
尽管心灵在通过原因或结果进行它的推理时，其视野超出了它所见到的或所记忆的那些对象之外，但是，它绝不能完全不再看见那些对象，或者仅仅依据它自己的观念进行推理，而是必须在推理中混合一些印象，或者至少是与印象相当的记忆的观念。
当我们从原因推断出结果时，我们必须建立这些原因的存在；而要做到这一点，仅仅有两条路径：要么根据我们的记忆或感官的直接知觉，要么根据由其他原因而来的推论；而这些其他的原因我们又必须以相同的方式加以确定，要么是根据当前的印象，要么是根据由它们的原因而来的推论，按照这样的推论一直进行下去，直到我们到达我们能够看见或记忆起的某个对象为止。对我们而言，不可能把我们的推理无限地进行下去；唯一能使我们的一169一

that can stop them, is an impression of the memory or senses, beyond
which there is no room for doubt or enquiry.
To give an instance of this, we may chuse any point of history,
and consider for what reason we either believe or reject it. Thus we
believe that CAESAR was kill' d in the senate-house on the ides of
March;and that because this fact is establish'd on the unanimous
testimony of historians, who agree to assign this precise time and
place to that event. Here are certain characters and letters present ei-
ther to our memory or senses; which characters we likewise remember
to have been us’ d as the signs of certain ideas ,and these ideas were
either in the minds of such as were immediately present at that action,
and receiv′ d the ideas directly from its existence; or they were
deriv′ d from the testimony of others, and that again from another tes-
timony, by a visible gradation, 'till we arrive at those who were eye-
witnesses and spectators of the event. ^ Tis obvious all this chain of ar-
gument or connexion of causes and effects, is at first founded on those
characters or letters, which are seen or remember' d, and that without
the authority either of the memory or senses our whole reasoning
wou' d be chimerical and without foundation. Every link of the chain
wou' d in that case hang upon another; but there wou' d not be any
thing fix' d to one end of it, capable of sustaining the whole; and
consequently there wou’ d be no belief nor evidence. And this actually
is the case with all hypothetical arguments, or reasonings upon a sup-
position ;there being in them, neither any present impression, nor be-
lief of a real existence.
I need not observe, that'tis no just objection to the present doc
trine, that we can reason upon our past conclusions or principles,
without having recourse to those impressions, from which they first a-
rose. For even supposing these impressions shou’ d be entirely effac′ d
from the memory, the conviction they produc’ d may still remain;
and’'tis equally true, that all reasonings concerning causes and effects
are originally deriv' d from some impression;in the same manner,
—170—

推理得以停止的就是一个记忆或感官的印象，如果超出了这些印象以外，就不再有怀疑或探究的空间。
要在这方面给出一个例子，我们可以选择历史上的任何一点，并且考察我们基于什么理由去相信或者否决它。例如，我们相信恺撒是三月十五日在元老院被杀死，这是由于这个事实是建立在历史学家的一致证据上面的，而这些历史学家都同意将这个精确的时间和地点指派给那一事件。在这里，有某些字符和文字呈现于我们的记忆或感官之前，我们同样记得这些字符曾经被用作是某些观念的记号；并且这些观念或者是在行刺时就立刻呈现于心灵中，并且由于它的存在而直接获得这些观念，或者是来自于别人的证据，而这种证据又是根据别的证据而来的，按照这种可见的顺序推进，直到我们达到那些事件的目击者为止。显然，
所有的论证系列或因果联系首先是建立在所见过的或所记忆的那些字符或文字上面的；如果没有记忆或感官的威信，我们的整个推理都将成为空想而没有根据。那个系列中的每一个环节都要依赖于那种情况下的另一个环节；但是，这个系列的一头并不固定于能够支持全部系列的任何东西上面，因此也就没有信念和证据。实际上，所有假设的论证或建立在假定上面的推理都是这种情形；在它们中间，既没有先前的印象，也没有对一个真实的存在的信念。
我不必说，对自前的学说做出如下的反驳是不恰当的，即认为我们能够根据过去的结论或原理进行推论，而不必求助于最初产生这些结论的那些印象。因为，即使假定这些印象已经在记忆中完全消失了，它们所产生的信念仍然可以保留；同样正确的是，关于原因和结果的所有推理最初都是源自于某种印象，正如
—171一

as the assurance of a demonstration proceds always from a compari-
son of ideas, tho’it may continue after the comparison is forgot.
SECTION V.Of The Impressions Of
TheSensesAnd Memory.
In this kind of reasoning, then, from causation, we employ ma-
terials, which are of a mix′ d and heterogeneous nature, and which,
however connected, are yet essentially different from each other. All
our arguments concerming causes and effects consist both of an im-
pression of the memory or senses, and of the idea of that existence,
which produces the object of the impression, or is produc′ d by it.
Here therefore we have three things to explain, viz. First, The origi-
nal impression. Secondly, The transition to the idea of the connected
cause or effect. Thirdly, The nature and qualities of that idea.
As to those impressions, which arise from the senses, their ulti-
mate cause is, in my opinion, perfectly inexplicable by human rea-
son, and 'twill always be impossible to decide with certainty, wheth-
er they arise immediately from the object, or are produc’d by the cre
ative power of the mind, or are deriv' d from the author of our being.
Nor is such a question any way material to our present purpose. We
may draw inferences from the coherence of our perceptions, whether
they be true or false; whether they represent nature justly, or be mere
illusions of the senses.
When we search for the characteristic, which distinguishes the
memory from the imagination, we must immediately perceive, that it
cannot lie in the simple ideas it presents to us; since both these facul-
ties borrow their simple ideas from the impressions, and can never go
beyond these original perceptions. These faculties are as little distin-
guish′ d from each other by the arrangement of their complex ideas. For

某种论证的担保总是来自于观念的比较一样，虽然比较被遗忘后，担保却仍然可以继续存在。
